pharm: Camptothecin topoisomerase I inhibitor; prodrug metabolized to active SN-38
summary: Irinotecan is an intravenous camptothecin-derivative topoisomerase I inhibitor used for metastatic colorectal cancer, either first-line with 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin or for disease that has progressed after fluorouracil-based therapy. It is a prodrug converted to the potent active metabolite SN-38. It carries a boxed warning for severe diarrhea (early cholinergic and dangerous late diarrhea) and severe myelosuppression, which must be managed aggressively.
indications: First-line therapy of metastatic colorectal cancer in combination with 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin
Metastatic colorectal cancer that has recurred or progressed after fluorouracil-based therapy

dosage.d: 125 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, 15, 22 with leucovorin and 5-FU
180 mg/m2 on days 1, 15, 29 with leucovorin and 5-FU

dosage.n: Reduce for UGT1A1*28 homozygotes / prior toxicity

admin: Administer as a 90-minute IV infusion by clinicians experienced in chemotherapy
Premedicate with antiemetics; have atropine available for cholinergic symptoms
Treat early diarrhea and cholinergic symptoms with atropine; treat late diarrhea promptly with loperamide
Withhold/reduce dose for severe diarrhea or neutropenia
Consider reduced starting dose in patients homozygous for UGT1A1*28
moa: Irinotecan and its active metabolite SN-38 bind the topoisomerase I-DNA complex, preventing re-ligation of single-strand breaks; collision with the replication fork causes lethal double-strand DNA damage (S-phase cytotoxicity).
preg: Can cause fetal harm based on mechanism and animal data; avoid in pregnancy and advise effective contraception.
lact: SN-38 found in animal milk; discontinue breastfeeding during therapy and for a period after.
renal: No formal dose adjustment; not recommended in patients on dialysis. Use with caution.
hepatic: Patients with elevated bilirubin have reduced SN-38 clearance and greater neutropenia risk; do not use with bilirubin above defined thresholds.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenytoin, St. John's wort) — reduce active metabolite, lower efficacy; avoid
Strong CYP3A4/UGT1A1 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole) — increase exposure and toxicity; avoid
moderate: Prochlorperazine — increased akathisia when same day
interactions.food: Not applicable (parenteral); avoid St. John's wort.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor UGT1A1 genotype where dosing decisions depend on it.

serious: Severe, life-threatening late diarrhea with dehydration
Severe neutropenia / neutropenic fever and sepsis
Colitis / ileus, bowel obstruction and rare GI perforation

monitoring: Complete blood count before each dose
counsel: Start loperamide at the first loose stool after the early period and continue per instructions
Drink plenty of fluids; report diarrhea that does not stop or fever
Early cramping, sweating or watery eyes during infusion are treated with atropine
Report fever, chills or signs of infection immediately
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed during treatment
pk: Cytotoxic over the cell cycle after conversion to SN-38
Effects extend across the dosing cycle
Vials 15-30 C (59-86 F), protect from light
pearls: Boxed warning: severe diarrhea and severe myelosuppression
Early diarrhea is cholinergic and responds to atropine; late diarrhea is dangerous and requires prompt high-dose loperamide
UGT1A1*28 homozygotes have higher SN-38 exposure and severe neutropenia risk — consider a reduced starting dose
Withhold for any patient with active diarrhea or neutropenia until resolved
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers (including St. John's wort) and inhibitors
missed: Doses are scheduled within a chemotherapy protocol and managed by the oncology team; missed or delayed infusions are not self-administered.
overdose: No antidote. Overdose intensifies diarrhea and myelosuppression. Provide maximal supportive care: aggressive antidiarrheal/loperamide therapy, fluids and electrolytes, and management of neutropenia and infection.
